messages:
Priya: CI alerted me to a typing regression in sample-app after the autogen change that lets enums accept unknown values as raw strings. mypy errors on the model field assignment.
Marco: can you paste the mypy output?
Priya:
```
src/models/order.py:42: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "str | None", variable has type "OrderStatus | None")  [assignment]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 14 source files)
```
Jules: I ran into this locally. The generator now emits a plain str for open enums to avoid ValueError at runtime, but static types no longer reflect the enum possibility.
Marco: proposal: generated models should annotate open enums as `Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]` and include a pydantic `@validator(..., pre=True)` that tries `OrderStatus(v)` then falls back to the raw str. That way callers and linters see both cases.
Priya: yep. important compatibility notes: 1) avoid PEP 604 union syntax to not require `from __future__ import annotations` for projects targeting 3.8; 2) ensure `Union` and `Optional` are imported from `typing` in generated files.
Theo: pyright users will thank you if the union is explicit. Pyright's inference and mypy's are subtly different; an explicit Union keeps both happy. Also mention pyright config in the PR so customers know we considered it.
Jules: adding a short generated-file comment explaining why we allow raw strings (server forward-compat) and showing the validator pattern helps downstream maintainers. Example generator output I plan to land:
```
from typing import Optional, Union

class Order(BaseModel):
    status: Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]] = None

    @validator('status', pre=True, always=True)
    def _coerce_status(cls, v):
        if v is None:
            return v
        try:
            return OrderStatus(v)
        except ValueError:
            return v  # unknown values preserved as raw str for forward compatibility
```
Priya: also add a typing test that uses `reveal_type` and an async consumption pattern. Async iterators can sometimes surface different inference issues. Example test sketch:
```
async def test_stream_status_typing(client):
    async for order in client.stream_orders():
        reveal_type(order.status)  # mypy: reveal_type -> "Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]"
        assert isinstance(order.status, (OrderStatus, str, type(None)))
        break
```
Marco: good. CI should run both mypy and pyright checks on sample-app. CI-bot: sample-app/mypy-check failed on branch enum-coerce-1987654321  https://ci.internal/runs/6242  logs attached.
Theo: when you open the PR call out that we intentionally avoided `from __future__ import annotations` to prevent forcing annotation postponement into user code; we can revisit later if we want PEP 563 style globally.
Jules: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autogen/pull/4399  includes generator change, sample-app typing/async test, and a note in generated files.
CI-bot: PR 4399 CI: mypy+pyright checks passed, unit tests passed. Merged into main at 1987654441.
Priya: merging looks good. I'll trigger a smoke-run against quickstart and playground to make sure no downstream surprises.
Marco: thanks all. This should avoid runtime crashes while keeping types informative. :thumbsup:
